segment.name: A newsletter writer or solo product maker who needs a page collecting email addresses before a launch date they have already announced
segment.organization: Pre-revenue solo project or one-person newsletter; no marketing team, no dedicated budget line
segment.workflow: Announces a date publicly, then needs somewhere to send attention; wires a signup form on a one-pager into the email tool they already pay for rather than standing up hosting, a form backend and a certificate by hand
segment.need: A page worth sending traffic to this week that deposits names and emails into the existing list tool, on their own domain, without a monthly bill
segment.buyer_role: The founder or writer, spending personal money; the decision is made in minutes at a sub-50-dollar-a-year price point
segment.user_role: The same person — they build the page and wire the form themselves
segment.current_alternative: The email provider's own hosted signup page, a dedicated waitlist tool, a free bio link, or a hand-rolled static page on Netlify or GitHub Pages with a third-party form

counterevidence_summary: Makers in this audience describe building the whole capture path themselves at zero cost except the domain. — A technically capable segment that already assembles free alternatives is a substantial buying obstacle, not merely an objection to handle in copy. Review before prioritising.

The stated decision criteria for this job are a free tier and fast setup. — Price-to-zero is named as a primary filter by a member of the audience, which directly contests the paid-plan purchase hypothesis. Review before prioritising.

A third-party pricing breakdown confirms forms are unavailable below the mid tier, which is the segment's anticipated objection. — The gate is real and publicly documented, but it is resolved by a $19 annual tier rather than being an unmet requirement. Minor condition; does not exclude this audience.
reasons: A solo maker in the fetched Indie Hackers thread states they used this product for a pre-launch landing page alongside a separate waitlist tool, which is an observed account of this audience using the product (though not of paying for it).
The same comment gives the buying logic the candidate hypothesises — the absence of monthly subscriptions was the stated reason for the choice.

Product truth covers the required capabilities: signup forms into the named email platforms (fact_9e623b882e57164b, fact_17afc28e667c2955), custom domains (fact_e18bb6f900ed3965) and SSL (fact_bdf6c3f1a677f1ee); the tier gates the candidate worries about are also in product truth (signup forms from Pro Standard, custom and payment-enabled forms on Pro Plus).

Indie Hackers threads are a concrete public venue where this exact tool-choice question is asked and answered by named participants, so both findability and reachability are established for this pass.
unknowns: Whether any maker in this segment has paid for a plan rather than publishing on the free tier
Whether the 'announced launch date' trigger in the candidate definition drives the choice, since neither thread mentions a dated announcement
How many of these makers hit the Pro Standard form gate and upgrade versus switching to a free form backend
Review the counterevidence before prioritising this audience.

segment.who: Indie hackers, solo SaaS makers, newsletter writers and self-publishing authors in the window between announcement and launch
segment.why_them: Hypothesis: in public builder forums this exact job is discussed as a tool choice with a named price, and the recurring framing is the fastest way to capture emails without a monthly subscription — which matches an annual, form-integrated one-pager more closely than a full site builder. The decision window is days, because the audience arrives before the infrastructure.
segment.trigger: A launch or publication date is announced publicly, or a post travels further than expected and there is nowhere to capture the readers
pains: Interest arrives before infrastructure; a page plus a form plus a domain plus SSL is not a this-week job by hand
They refuse a second place to manage subscribers — whatever they build must write into the list tool they already use
They build on the free tier and only then discover the signup form needs a paid tier, at the exact moment they are trying to ship
Waitlist and page tooling is mostly priced monthly, which is uneconomic for a page that matters for six weeks
segment.objection: The thing I actually need will turn out to be on a higher tier — I'll pay for the cheapest plan, then find forms need the next one, then find custom forms and payments need the one above that.
segment.angle: Optional hypothesis: name the gates before they are hit (signup forms from Pro Standard; custom and payment-enabled forms on Pro Plus) and point at the 7-day trial that needs no card, since this reader's objection is a pricing-structure suspicion rather than a capability doubt.
segment.basis: Refresh of an existing inferred segment; name and definition unchanged. Now partly supported by public builder-forum threads where practitioners describe choosing a one-pager plus an email-platform integration for pre-launch capture and explicitly value the absence of a monthly subscription. Counterevidence: free hosted waitlist tools and email providers' own landing pages cover the same job at zero cost. Missing: any first-party customer evidence for this product, and anything on consent or data-processing terms for forms, which this buyer may ask about.

researchability_reasons: 6 useful observable signals and 5 specific research venues.
The audience is anchored in a concrete workflow or situation.
A clear trigger narrows the evidence to look for.

required_structural_signals.description: One-person project with no marketing headcount and no agency
Already runs a list on a named email service they intend to keep

required_workflow_signals.description: A date has been stated publicly, creating a dated capture need
The current funnel ends at a hosted provider form or a social post

optional_signals.description: Current capture page sits on someone else's domain
Already instruments pages with Plausible, GA or Matomo
Pre-orders or paid tiers already taken via a payment link

hard_disqualifiers.description: Requires a blog, docs or many indexable URLs at launch
Tooling must pass vendor review, DPAs or SSO requirements

excluded_subsegments: funded startups with a marketing team
agencies buying on behalf of clients at scale
